A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TOHA, with matching core algorithms and substantial overlapping experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, transfer evaluations, ablations, runtime measurements, and annotation-validation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional HotpotQA, baseline-comparison, copying-head, response-length, and annotator-agreement results.

M1.justification: The attention-graph construction, prompt-edge zeroing, normalized divergence, head ranking, AUROC-based head-count selection, and prediction averaging remain unchanged. The increased head cap is an experimental hyperparameter change; the new information-theoretic interpretation does not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V3 adds HotpotQA's multi-hop, multi-document QA scenario for Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B (Table 3). This is a focused extension within RAG hallucination detection; the original MS MARCO, CNN/DM plus Recent News, CoQA, SQuAD, and XSum coverage remains.

E2.justification: ReDEEP joins the retained seven detector baselines in Tables 1–2 and receives an additional entire-RAGTruth comparison in Table 7. The runtime comparison also replaces perplexity with max entropy. LapEigVals and other newly cited methods are not established as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 specifies a 60/15/25 split and 150 annotated selection/tuning samples; v3 specifies 25% test data and 100 validation samples. The head cap increases from six to ten. V3 introduces comparisons using one additional SelfCheckGPT generation and five for semantic entropy/EigenScore, retaining 20-generation comparisons in Tables 5–6. Several dataset sample counts also change (v2 Table 8; v3 Table 15).

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of prompt-edge zeroing, head-count sensitivity, copying-head associations, and single-word response performance, plus response-length distributions. V2's explicit removal-of-<s> ablation disappears. Probe-size experiments replace CNN/DM with SQuAD, while the existing supervised feature comparisons and alternative head-selection analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages and uncertainty alongside benchmark scores. V3 specifies that runs use different splits and adds targeted statistical reporting: independent-sample transferability t-tests (Table 9), runtime uncertainty (Figure 4a), and cross-annotator agreement with means and standard deviations (Table 14). No increase in run count is stated.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, transfer values, and timings are extensively replaced. For example, reported Mistral-7B TOHA AUROC on SQuAD changes from 0.84±0.01 to 0.96±0.01 under revised settings, so this is not an established same-setting gain. New HotpotQA AUROCs are 0.71±0.08 and 0.80±0.03 for Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B. The supervised-feature and GPT-4o annotation-validation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 introduces an MST-based entropy estimate and claimed entropy/perplexity lower bounds connecting divergence to response novelty. Existing MSF, stability, exact-sequence, and zero-divergence properties and proofs are largely retained and reorganized in Appendix D. V2's maximum-bar-length norm definition and its bound are removed.

C1.justification: V3 promotes the interpretation of divergence as response novelty to an explicit central contribution and adds copying-head associations to the introduction and conclusion. V2 emphasized weak context connections, stability, and the importance of <s>. The sufficient-head claim changes from six to ten, and performance wording narrows from all benchmarks to multiple benchmarks.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations involving informational novelty, noise from prompt-internal connections, and copying behavior. Appendix B.5 interprets short-response failures through graph degeneration and long-response difficulty through diluted hallucination signals. V2's explicit limitation requiring context containing the correct answer is removed; model-specific, multimodal, and adversarial limitations remain.

D1.justification: The documented topology library changes from ripser++ to ripser, and the code-link target changes. V3 newly specifies evaluate version 0.4.6 and L1 regularization for the retained feature classifiers. It omits v2's detailed HaloScope unlabeled-data and extra-CoQA-generation instructions; that omission does not establish that those procedures stopped.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand positioning against recent attention-based approaches, including ReDEEP, LapEigVals, and uncertainty-aware heads. New copying-head and MST-entropy literature supports the revised mechanism and theoretical narrative. Several earlier motivation citations disappear, beyond bibliographic updates or relocation.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, method, results, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Method exposition gains separate definition, geometry, and perplexity subsections; experiments become Sections 4.1–4.4. Related work moves to Appendix A, other appendices are reordered, and affiliations and correspondence details change.

P2.justification: V3 removes the opening heatmaps, rearranges and relabels head-separation and probe/transfer plots, annotates the MSF illustration, and combines revised timing displays with head-count plots. It adds copying and response-length figures and several experimental/statistical tables. Annotation-validation averages are merged into the main table instead of displayed separately.

improvement.justification: HotpotQA, ReDEEP, additional ablations, and annotator-agreement reporting broaden the empirical support. However, the new central novelty claim relies on an unresolved entropy/perplexity derivation: Section 3.3 switches the subtracted prompt term to a response term without explanation. Removing v2's correct-context limitation also weakens applicability qualifications. These benefits and substantive weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
